<p>Every team we talk to wants AI teammates, but doesn't know how to actually put one to work. Maybe you've tried homebrewing OpenClaw or Hermes. The two usual options both whiff: traditional automation (UiPath) makes you sign up for a months-long integration project before it does one useful thing, and AI "assistants" hand you a wall of text, and you still go do the work yourself.</p>
<p><strong>Ace is different.</strong> You onboard it like any new hire, and it shows up where the work happens:</p>
<p>• Forward it an email or cc its own inbox, and the draft lands in your Drive with the judgment calls left as comments.</p>
<p>• @Ace in Slack after a call, and the summary + action items land on the opportunity.</p>
<p>• Text it between meetings ("move Thursday to Friday and tell them why"), and it updates the invite, emails everyone, and confirms.</p>
<p>• Ping it in a doc comment, or have it make a call on its own line.</p>
<p>What comes back is finished work: CRM updated, email sent, invoice reconciled. When it hits a real fork in the road, it hands you the open questions instead of guessing.</p>
<p><strong>Why trust it?</strong> We spent two years automating high-volume work in mortgage, lending, and insurance, where a wrong answer is a compliance problem. Ace pairs a deterministic engine for must-be-identical work with AI for the fuzzy stuff. Every run is logged step by step, you set what needs approval, and you can revoke access like any employee's. SOC 2, encrypted credentials, role-based access.</p>
